chunk_map.heading: The verifier decides pass without you
Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "One run, plotted": line 200: "**A check is a position fix**" — a bolded 6-word declarative clause (subject-verb-complement), over the ≲5-word handle cap and the exact "never a whole lead sentence" shape the rule bans, independent of the maintainer's accept-with-note. chunk 6 "Hooks for must-happen, prompts for taste": line 232: "**Must happen goes in a hook**" — same 6-word whole-clause-bold shape; maintainer block labels it a kept "(governor)" handle, but the governor category still has to be a short handle per the rule's own text, not a full sentence. (Chunk 2's "Reference artefact" / "plan.md" pair, flagged in the prior run, is NOT re-flagged here: both are short noun-phrase handles under 5 words each, and two named pattern-pieces on one slide fit the explicit "law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law" exception cleanly — no separate maintainer sign-off needed for that one.)
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim these two to a short noun-phrase handle (e.g. bold just "position fix" / "hook") or drop the bold and let the sentence run plain — both currently repeat the pre-2026-07-09 whole-sentence-bold pattern the rest of the pass removed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
